# Mise & Meal architecture

- Frontend: responsive vanilla JavaScript SPA. `app.js` renders product surfaces; `ingredients.js` owns catalogue search, selection, and shared unit options.
- Backend and authentication: Supabase PostgreSQL and Supabase Auth through `supabase-client.js`. Browser configuration uses a publishable key, never a service-role key. The Ruby build supports public configuration from environment variables or `supabase-config.local.js`.
- Source of truth: `db/supabase/001` through `007`. `db/schema.sql` is a legacy SQLite/D1 design and is not used by the current browser persistence layer. Existing hosting D1 metadata is retained, not migrated.
- Shared catalogue: `ingredients.id` is referenced by `inventory.ingredient_id` and `recipe_ingredients.ingredient_id`. Authenticated users read shared starter records and their own custom records. Migration 007 enables owner-only custom creation/editing; shared rows remain protected. The picker supports inline creation, and Inventory → Manage ingredients provides a catalogue editor. Names are presentation data; IDs are persisted identity.
- Inventory: one record per user and ingredient. RLS restricts all operations to its owner. Quantity, entered unit, storage location, threshold, expiry and notes belong to inventory. Default units belong to the catalogue and are suggestions only.
- Recipes: owned through `recipes.user_id`; recipe ingredient RLS checks parent ownership. Recipe creation is currently multiple requests with compensating deletion on failure, not an atomic database transaction. Recipe editing uses the atomic `update_recipe` RPC installed by migration 006. Deletion cascades to recipe ingredients and removes references from the current browser plan; shopping and inventory remain unchanged. Uploaded covers may remain orphaned after failures, replacements, or deletion.
- Units: entered units are preserved. Cooking compares matching ingredient IDs and converts g/kg, ml/l and piece/pcs; incompatible units require manual review. Exact quantities remain the existing UI model; ingredient identity is independent of quantities and supports a later nullable-quantity/status migration.
- Legacy limitations: inventory display state remains name-keyed; cooking matches stable IDs when available. Planner/shopping state is in localStorage under per-user keys; it does not sync across devices. Unowned legacy shared state is preserved but not automatically assigned to any account. Account changes clear rendered kitchen state and stale database loads are ignored. Recipes/inventory are stored in Supabase under RLS.

See `db/CANONICAL_INGREDIENTS.md` for rollout, data review and validation.

Recipe editor rollout: apply `db/supabase/006_recipe_edit.sql` in Supabase before deploying. No live database changes are performed by the local build. Verify edits (including ingredient replacement), ownership isolation and deletion in authenticated sessions.

Catalogue rollout: run `007_editable_ingredient_catalogue.sql` before deploying the new frontend. It includes missing 004 columns/index setup; normalized-name collisions abort without data loss. Run 005 after 007 to populate shared starter ingredients including Pasta. If 004 was never applied, do not run it after 007. Shared entries retain existing IDs; user edits preserve custom ingredient IDs and saved units. Catalogue search errors are shown separately from empty results.
